description: An example legal code for a small town: EXAMPLE CONTENT, not a default (D18). A world includes it deliberately. It holds no sum of money and no place's figure: a law whose substance is figures is written from a schedule (schedules.json) with the place's own, and a sum a law names stands here as {name} and is written in as the world writes its money, from its profile, when the world is made. Each statement is a record with plain text, an Institutional Grammar breakdown (who / may-must-must not / what / when / or else) and, where machine-checkable, a formal CEL condition used by code-run institutions and by measurement, never by the kernel.

records.author: genesis
records.text: The town is governed by an elected mayor and council. The council makes the town's laws by majority vote, on proposals from the mayor or any councillor. The mayor proposes each year's budget and the council adopts it before the year begins. The finance office pays the town's wages and bills within the budget adopted for the year. While a year has no adopted budget, the finance office may go on paying what the town is already bound to pay (wages under agreements in force, and what falls due under agreements and laws made before the year began), at no more each month than a twelfth of the budget last adopted; nothing new is undertaken until the council adopts the year's budget, which then covers the whole year, what was paid in the meantime included. The planning office decides building permits under the planning laws. The building inspector inspects sites and reports breaches.

records.author: genesis
records.text: Land and buildings belong to whoever the land registry records as their owner. No one may build on, occupy or demolish another's property without the owner's agreement. Or else: the owner may seek removal and damages through the council.

adico.aim: build on, occupy or demolish another's property

records.author: genesis
records.text: No building may be built anywhere in town without a permit from the planning office. Or else: a fine of {fine} and an order to demolish.

adico.condition: without a planning permit for that parcel
adico.or_else: a fine of {fine} and a demolition order

records.author: genesis
records.text: When someone dies, their money passes to their partner; if they have none, in equal shares to their adult children; if none, to the town. A death is registered with the town's registry, and a bank that learns of it pays no more from the dead person's accounts except to settle the estate.

adico.attribute: the estate of someone who has died
adico.aim: pass to their partner, else their adult children equally, else the town
